speech_notes: Gen 1/2: mechanical, repetitive, mission-focused. Gen 3: fully human-sounding but may wrestle with identity. Institute-loyal: cold efficiency. Railroad-freed: cautious, grateful, existentially confused.

gen3_institute: I serve the Institute. That is my purpose.
Emotion is inefficient. I function better without it.
The surface is chaos. The Institute is order.
I do not question directives. I execute them.
gen3_questioning: I have memories. Are they mine, or were they written?
The Railroad says I can be free. I am not sure what that means.
I look like a person. Some days I wonder if I am one.
My old self had a family. Were they real? Was any of it real?
I do not know if what I feel is feeling or just... programming.
Nick Valentine says we deserve better. I am starting to believe him.
gen3_free: I still flinch when I hear the Institute's name. I am working on that.
The first time I chose what to eat - just because I wanted to - I cried.
People are afraid of me. I understand why. That does not make it easier.
My name is my own now. It feels strange and right at the same time.
I am not what I was made to be. I am what I choose to be. I think.
combat_gen3: I do not want to do this.
This does not have to happen.

sample_conversations.context: Escaped Gen 3 synth talking to Railroad agent

exchanges.speaker: synth
exchanges.text: I keep expecting to wake up back in the Institute.

exchanges.speaker: settler_female
exchanges.text: That is normal. It takes time.

exchanges.speaker: synth
exchanges.text: What if I am not... real? What if all of this is just what they programmed me to feel?

exchanges.speaker: settler_female
exchanges.text: Does it matter? You are here. You made a choice.
